messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Alignment Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | Ed | discourse marker “and” linking to previous narration | **Kaj** | “and” | OK | | ecco | exclamatory pointer “lo!” drawing attention | **jen** | “here/lo!” | OK | | quasi | degree adverb “almost” | **preskaŭ** | “almost” | OK | | al | preposition “at” (spatial) | **ĉe** | “at” | OK | | cominciar | noun “beginning” (of the steep) | **komenco** | “beginning” | OK | | de | genitive preposition “of” | **de** | “of” | OK | | l'erta | noun phrase “the steep (path)” | **kruta vojo** | “steep road” | OK | | una | indefinite article introducing a new referent | **unu** | “a / one” | OK | | lonza | noun “she‑leopard” | **leopardo** | “leopard” | OK | | leggera | adjective “light (in weight/appearance)” | **malpeza** | “light” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **kaj** | “and” | OK | | presta | adjective “nimble, quick” | **rapida** | “fast/quick” | OK | | molto | intensifier “very” | **tre** | “very” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which/that” | **kiu** | “who/which” | OK | | di | preposition “with” (instrument) | **per** | “by/with” | OK | | pel | noun “coat / fur” | **mantelo** | “coat” | OK | | macolato | past participle used adjectivally “spotted” | **makulita** | “spotted” | OK | | era | imperfect copula “was” | **estis** | “was” | OK | | coverta | passive past participle “covered” | **kovrita** | “covered” | OK |
### Issues Detected - **None.** All source tokens have been rendered in the Esperanto translation; no token is missing, incorrectly translated, grammatically mismatched, or unnecessarily added.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Esperanto script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 31: - Original: **Kaj jen preskaŭ ĉe la komenco de la kruta vojo,** - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 32: - Original: **unu leopardo malpeza kaj tre rapida,** - Issue: **UNNECESSARY** – the indefinite article “unu” is not required in Esperanto. - Corrected: **leopardo malpeza kaj tre rapida,**
- Line 33: - Original: **kiu estis kovrita per makulita mantelo;** - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
``` Kaj jen preskaŭ ĉe la komenco de la kruta vojo, leopardo malpeza kaj tre rapida, kiu estis kovrita per makulita mantelo; ```
